topics.topic: Whether all_projects alone grants global publication authority
questions: Does `scope_mode = all_projects` itself authorize every active project, or must a global producer also hold a separate explicitly granted global capability or project-access grant?
Does `all_projects` itself confer global publication scope, or must the principal also receive a distinct explicitly granted global capability?
Is selecting `scope_mode = all_projects` sufficient for global publication, or must the principal also receive a distinct explicitly granted global capability?

quotes:
With
  `all_projects` the scope mode alone admits an import for any project the
  Registry reports active; no grant is consulted and no further capability
  is needed.
judgement.divergence: An all-projects producer without a separate global-capability grant is either allowed to import for every active Registry project or rejected for lacking that additional grant; the producer and configuring administrator notice.
judgement.why: State 0 requires an explicitly granted global capability, while M13 says the all_projects scope mode needs no further capability.

events: The authenticated producer submits a valid snapshot publication for P.
outcomes: M13 admits the import because all_projects alone supplies project scope and P is active.
State 0 refuses the import because the principal lacks the separately explicitly granted global capability.

Does a successful first-administrator bootstrap create an AuditRecord?

judgement.why: The topic is the same first-administrator bootstrap audit question already decided in P6, and its quoted State 1 passage has not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether first-administrator bootstrap creates an audit record
quotes:
The first-administrator bootstrap of R0-07 is no exception: it writes one
  `staff.create` record with actor kind `system`, no actor, no project and
  the new `staff_id` as entity; the email and password it was given appear
  in no record.
precedent.why: State 1 explicitly requires the bootstrap audit and clarifies that R0-07's non-auditing rule applies to the supplied email and password.

topics.topic: Creation and persistence of candidate sections needed for pre-activation reallocation
questions: Which product action creates the candidate version’s SectionPlans and unmatched PortalSections early enough for operators to target them during the required pre-activation reallocation, and do those records survive a refused activation?
How can an operator reallocate to an unmatched section before activation if that section and its plan are created only by activation?

quotes:
Activation of an imported version creates plans by `source_key` linking:
matched keys reuse the existing `PortalSection` (rename allowed), unmatched
source sections create new `PortalSection` records.

Sections of the previous
version absent from the new one keep their identity and history; their
allocations would be *unresolved against the new version* (a derived state,
not a stored flag), so they must be explicitly re-allocated by an operator
before that version can be activated: activation is refused while any is
unresolved (accepted `activate_budget_version`).

In the running service no operation creates an imported budget version
(Q11, deferred), so this linking never runs; it describes the design Q11
starts from.

The State 0 "explicit mapping" of existing allocations is, in
the running service, the staff re-allocation of an expense (its whole
allocation set replaced by explicit instructions to sections of the
project, M29); activation of a version is refused while any section
allocation would be unresolved against it, and no other mapping operation
exists.
judgement.divergence: One implementation materializes the imported version's plans and unmatched PortalSections before activation, allowing the operator to target them during reallocation; another creates them only inside activation, which refuses before they persist, leaving the operator unable to target them. The operator preparing the transition notices.
judgement.why: The texts require pre-activation reallocation to candidate sections but assign creation of those sections to activation and name no earlier creating action.

witness.initial: Project P has an active manual version with section O, an expense E allocated to O, and an accepted snapshot containing only unmatched source section N.
events: An authorized staff member reviews the accepted imported version for activation.
The staff member attempts to replace E's allocations with an allocation targeting N.
The staff member attempts to activate the imported version.
outcomes: The implementation materializes N and its SectionPlan with the inactive candidate, so E can be reallocated to N and activation can succeed.
The implementation creates N only during activation, but activation refuses while E remains allocated to O and persists nothing, so N never becomes an available reallocation target.
witness.observer: The staff member preparing the budget transition.
basis:
existing allocations require explicit mapping to the sections of the newly
  activated version; matching stable section identifiers may link
  automatically; a renamed section with the same stable identifier remains
  the same section; sections without a stable correspondence require manual
  mapping; matching by display name alone is forbidden;

- **Rules:** the sum of an expense's allocations equals `total_amount`
  exactly; automatic proportional split is forbidden — every allocation is
  an explicit operator value; `section_id` must belong to the expense's
  project; re-allocation is a staff action on an active project.

provenance.quote: - import and activation are distinct actions: the producer imports, a human operator/administrator reviews and activates
existing allocations require explicit mapping to the sections of the newly activated version; matching stable section id

questions: Is an administrator’s StaffProjectAssignment intentionally inert, or must creating and revoking every StaffProjectAssignment grant and remove project access?

quotes:
An existing grant or assignment is not new access: it keeps giving read
access, also after the viewer receives a new access link or the staff
account is reinstated, because neither operation consults the Registry
(accepted notes `issue_viewer_access`, `change_staff_status`). Revoking an
existing viewer grant, staff assignment or producer grant does not consult the
Registry and succeeds for an archived project, also while the Registry is
unavailable, so archival never stands in for revocation (accepted notes
`revoke_viewer_project`, `revoke_staff_project_assignment`; Factory code
`application/viewer_access.py`, `application/staff_identity.py`,
`application/service_identity.py`).

The assignment operation accepts any
  existing staff account; an assignment naming an administrator has no
  effect, because authorization never consults assignments for the
  administrator role, and since no role ever changes (M05) an assignment
  never gains or loses effect through a role change.
judgement.divergence: Creating and revoking an administrator's StaffProjectAssignment either grants then removes project access, as State 0's assignment language requires, or has no authorization effect because the administrator always derives scope from the administrative area; the administrator making the read and the assignment manager notice.
judgement.why: State 0 says an existing staff assignment gives read access and can be revoked, whereas M07 says an assignment naming an administrator never affects authorization.

questions: When a known authenticated actor attempts a catalogued action but authorization rejects it before the owning use case changes or reads the target model, must that attempt create one rejected AuditRecord?

quotes:
- **Refusal.** An operation returns its output or raises one declared
  exception; a refusal is decided before the first write, so it writes
  nothing, except where its Errors say the rejection is itself recorded.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contract says a pre-write authorization refusal records nothing unless that operation's Errors explicitly declares the rejection recorded.

topics.topic: Disablement provenance after re-enabling a ServicePrincipal
questions: After `disabled → active`, are `disabled_at` and `disabled_by` cleared, retained as the most recent disablement, or represented through additional enablement facts?

quotes:
- **Fields:** `service_principal_id: UUID`, `name: str`,
  `source_type: ProducerSourceType` (closed catalog; initially
  `estimate_producer`), `status: PrincipalStatus (active | disabled)`,
  `scope_mode: ProducerScopeMode (all_projects | granted_projects)`
  `[closed-choice]`, `created_at`, `created_by`, `disabled_at | None`,
  `disabled_by | None`.

the only modification
  is the status change `active ↔ disabled` (disabling revokes every
  credential of the principal; re-enabling restores none of them, so a
  re-enabled principal needs a newly issued credential).

- `ServicePrincipalView` — `service_principal_id: UUID`, `name: str`,
  `source_type: ProducerSourceType`, `status: PrincipalStatus`,
  `scope_mode: ProducerScopeMode`, `created_at: datetime`,
  `disabled_at: datetime | None`.
judgement.divergence: Re-enabling either clears disabled_at and disabled_by as current-state provenance or retains the most recent disablement facts; an administrator reading ServicePrincipalView notices null versus the prior disablement timestamp.
judgement.why: The lifecycle permits re-enabling and exposes disablement provenance, but no passage defines those fields after the transition back to active.

witness.initial: ServicePrincipal S is active with disabled_at and disabled_by unset.
events: Administrator A disables S at time t1.
Administrator B re-enables S at time t2.
An administrator reads S through ServicePrincipalView.
outcomes: Re-enabling clears disabled_at and disabled_by, so the active view has disabled_at = null.
Re-enabling retains the most recent disablement provenance, so the active view has disabled_at = t1.
witness.observer: The administrator reading the service-principal view.
basis:
- **Created/modified by:** administrator. `name`, `source_type` and
  `scope_mode` are set at creation and never change; the only modification
  is the status change `active ↔ disabled` (disabling revokes every
  credential of the principal; re-enabling restores none of them, so a
  re-enabled principal needs a newly issued credential).

- `ServicePrincipalView` — `service_principal_id: UUID`, `name: str`,
  `source_type: ProducerSourceType`, `status: PrincipalStatus`,
  `scope_mode: ProducerScopeMode`, `created_at: datetime`,
  `disabled_at: datetime | None`.

quotes: The new active `ServicePrincipal` (the route answers its safe view).

topics.topic: Whether ServicePrincipal creation includes an initial credential and secret
questions: What records and one-time secret does the ServicePrincipal creation action create: only the principal, or the principal together with an initial ServiceCredential?

quotes:
`ServiceCredentialIssue`: the new `ServiceCredential` with the next
`key_version` and the secret in plaintext, returned once.
judgement.why: The later API makes principal creation write only the principal and audit, while the separate credential-issuance operation creates and returns the credential and one-time secret.

precedent.topic: ProducerProjectGrant eligibility for disabled or all-projects principals
quotes:
### Errors

Access-management failures; `ScopedNotFoundError` for a project the Registry
does not know or an unknown principal; `ArchivedProjectRejected` for an
inactive project; `AuthorizationRejected` for an existing active grant;
`RegistryBoundaryError`.
precedent.why: The later operation's closed failures impose no active-principal or granted_projects-scope precondition, so grants may be created for disabled and all-projects principals.
